subject: biology-hl
about: Original practice questions written for NevaIB from the IB guide's syllabus understandings and the school's unit order. Not IB past-paper questions, not publisher material and not IB markschemes: the marking points are written for self-marking. Organisms, experiments and data in data-response items are invented for practice.

items.stem: A hydrogen bond between water molecules forms between:
choices: Two hydrogen atoms of neighbouring water molecules sharing a pair of electrons covalently
The oxygen atoms of two neighbouring water molecules
An H⁺ ion and an OH⁻ ion in the liquid
A partially positive H on one molecule and a partially negative O on another
items.note: Polarity gives δ+ hydrogens and δ− oxygen; the attraction between them is a hydrogen bond (weaker than covalent).

choices: Water to dissolve sodium chloride
Water to be pulled up xylem under tension
Ice to float on liquid water
Water to stick to the xylem walls
items.note: Cohesion (water–water hydrogen bonds) keeps the column continuous. Adhesion is water sticking to other surfaces.

items.stem: Pond skaters can walk on water because of:
choices: Surface tension, caused by cohesion
Adhesion between water and their legs
The high specific heat capacity of water
Water being a good solvent
items.note: Hydrogen bonds at the surface resist being stretched, forming a surface "skin".

items.stem: Adhesion of water to cellulose in plant cell walls is important because it:
choices: Prevents water evaporating from the leaf surface by holding it tightly inside the cell walls
Makes the cellulose fibres dissolve in water
Draws water through cell walls and up narrow tubes by capillary action
Allows ions to cross the plasma membrane
items.note: Water is attracted to hydrophilic cellulose, moving through walls and into thin spaces (capillarity).

choices: A triglyceride (fat)
Glucose
Sodium chloride
An amino acid with a charged R group
items.note: Non-polar molecules cannot form hydrogen bonds with water. Glucose and ions are hydrophilic.

items.stem: Water's high specific heat capacity means that:
choices: Water heats up very quickly in sunlight, so shallow ponds become too hot for most organisms
Large bodies of water change temperature slowly, giving stable habitats
Water boils at a low temperature
Ice sinks to the bottom of lakes in winter
items.note: Much energy is needed to break hydrogen bonds before temperature rises, buffering aquatic habitats.

items.stem: Evaporation of sweat cools the body because:
choices: Water vapour reflects heat away from the skin
Sweat contains salts that absorb heat
Water has a low specific heat capacity
Breaking hydrogen bonds to evaporate water absorbs a lot of heat
items.note: Water's high latent heat of vaporisation removes much heat per gram evaporated.

items.stem: Why is blood plasma able to transport glucose and sodium ions, but cholesterol is carried in lipoproteins?
choices: Cholesterol molecules are too small to stay suspended in plasma without being bound to a carrier
Glucose and ions are carried bound to red blood cells
Glucose and ions are hydrophilic and dissolve; cholesterol is hydrophobic
Cholesterol reacts with water if it is not protected
items.note: Polar and charged substances dissolve; non-polar ones need carriers to travel in watery plasma.

items.stem: One hypothesis for the origin of Earth's water is that it was delivered by:
choices: Photosynthesis by the first cyanobacteria
Condensation of water from the Sun's outer layers
Asteroids and comets that collided with the early Earth
The breakdown of glucose in the first cells
items.note: Water-rich asteroids/comets are thought to have brought water. Earth's distance from the Sun let it stay liquid.

items.stem: The "Goldilocks zone" around a star is the region where:
choices: Planets have an atmosphere made of oxygen
Planets have the same mass as Earth
Life has been confirmed to exist
Temperatures allow liquid water to exist on a planet's surface
items.note: Liquid water is considered necessary for life as we know it, so the search for life focuses there.

items.stem: Ice is less dense than liquid water. The biological significance is that:
choices: Ice sinks to the bottom and keeps the lake bed cold, so bottom-dwelling animals stay dormant
Ice floats and insulates the water below, so aquatic life survives winter
Ice reflects heat into the water below the surface
Lakes freeze from the bottom upward, protecting the surface
items.note: Hydrogen bonds in ice hold molecules further apart. Floating ice insulates the liquid water beneath.

items.stem: Explain how the polarity of water molecules makes water a good solvent.
markscheme: Water molecules have δ− oxygen and δ+ hydrogens (1)
They are attracted to ions and polar molecules (1)
Water molecules surround each solute particle (hydration shell), separating them (1)
items.tactic: Start with the cause (polarity), finish with the consequence (dissolving).

items.stem: Compare the thermal properties of water and air as habitats for animals.
markscheme: Water has a much higher specific heat capacity than air (1)
Water temperature is more stable / changes slowly (1)
Water conducts heat away faster, so animals lose body heat more quickly in water (1)
Air temperature can fluctuate widely (day/night, seasons) (1)
items.tactic: Compare = paired statements about the same property.

items.stem: Explain why water's cohesion and adhesion are both needed for transport in xylem.
markscheme: Cohesion: hydrogen bonds between water molecules keep the column continuous (1)
Tension from transpiration is transmitted down the column (1)
Adhesion to the hydrophilic xylem walls supports the column and helps it rise (1)
items.tactic: Name both properties and say what each does separately.

items.stem:
(Invented data for practice.) Temperatures of a small pond and the air above it were recorded over 24 h in summer: air minimum 9 °C, maximum 31 °C; pond minimum 18 °C, maximum 23 °C.
(a) Calculate the temperature range for air and for pond water. (b) Explain the difference using a property of water. (c) Suggest one advantage of this for organisms living in the pond.
markscheme: (b) Water has a high specific heat capacity (1)
Much energy is needed to change its temperature because hydrogen bonds must be broken/formed (1)
(c) Stable temperature, so enzymes work near their optimum / organisms need fewer adaptations to temperature change (1)
items.tactic: Unfamiliar context: find the syllabus idea being tested, quote the data (with units) when you describe a trend, then explain it with that idea. One marking point per linked step.
